newsitem.title: FINLAND: MATIF SAYS OPEN OUTCRY TRADING BEATS ELECTRONIC.
newsitem.headline: MATIF SAYS OPEN OUTCRY TRADING BEATS ELECTRONIC.

text.p: French futures exchange MATIF will maintain open outcry trading in its main products, although this rules out taking remote members, MATIF deputy managing director Jaques Werren said on Thursday.

He told a seminar arraged by training institute IIR Finland that he did not expect the three main Europen futures exchanges, the UK's LIFFE, German DTH and MATIF, to converge despite Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU) which has led to convergence in financial markets.

"The German DTB's example is a good case (of electronic trading) ... the result of fully electronic trading does not tell that the advantage of electronic trading is that big over trading in a pit", Werren told Reuters on the sidelines of the seminar.
"Open outcry is an opportunity to really see what is happening," he added.
MATIF -- which has some 100 institutional members of which 50 are foreign and one, SE-Banken, Nordic -- aims to maintain its leading position in interest rate derivatives, he said.
It is now fourth in the world after the two Chicago exchanges and London's LIFFE.
Werren said he could imagine more Nordic members joining MATIF due to EMU, but noted that this would require a presence in Paris.

MATIF has hedged its future in EMU with two scenarios in mind -- one with not yield spreads and another where spreads prevail, maybe rise and get more volatile, he said, adding MATIF had products based on French goverment benchmarks and related yield spread products.
